transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hello. Well, I made the appointment because I just can't seem to turn off the worrying once it starts. It's a bit frustrating because I'll tell myself that I've already made my lists, checked the dates, and done everything I reasonably can about a situation... but my mind just keeps worrying anyway.
What kinds of things do you find yourself worrying about most often?

Well, it's a bit of a mix. My mind just keeps roaming, really. I'll be focused on the exhibition schedule, and then... well, then it shifts to my daughter's travel plans, or even just wondering whether the house gutters need fixing. It's mostly everyday things. But these small things start to feel as if they could unravel into something much bigger, and I just can't seem to stop thinking about them.
About how long have you been experiencing this persistent worrying?

I'd say it's been going on for about seven months now. It started shortly after a friend of mine passed away. I was trying to keep the projects we shared moving forward, and... well, that's when this constant worrying really seemed to start.
Have you noticed any physical muscle tension or tightness along with this constant worrying?

Yes, I definitely have. By the time evening comes around, my shoulders and neck are just... well, they're so tight. It feels like I've been holding myself braced all day. I actually catch myself clenching my jaw, too, usually when I'm just trying to sit and read, or when I'm planning out the activities for the garden center. It's just a constant tightness.
Have you been having any trouble falling or staying asleep since this began?

No, not really. I mean... my sleep has been pretty normal, actually. Once I finally get into bed, I don't seem to have much trouble falling asleep, and I generally sleep right through the night. It's really just during the day that my mind won't stop.
Do you frequently feel restless, keyed up, or on edge during the day?

Yes, I do. I often feel pretty wound up, even when I'm just sitting in my own living room. If I'm on a phone call, I'll catch myself tapping my fingers the whole time. Or I'll... well, I'll just get up to straighten something around the room, really just because sitting quietly makes me feel a bit jumpy.
Have you found that you get tired or fatigued more easily than usual during the day?

Yes, I have. It's a bit frustrating because, like I said, I sleep right through the night, but... well, I often wake up feeling as if I've already put in half a day. And then doing just normal things takes it out of me. By the time I finish watering the garden beds or sorting through papers for my book club, I just really need to sit down and gather myself. So, yes, I definitely feel tired much faster than I used to.

latest_inference.note: Patient meets full ICD-10 criteria for generalized anxiety disorder with excessive, uncontrollable worry for over 6 months across multiple everyday domains, accompanied by at least three associated symptoms (muscle tension, restlessness/keyed up, and easy fatigability).
